package_info.package_versions: Unknown (affects all sites using the compromised provider's code)
package_info.why_malicious: The JavaScript code distributed by a trusted media content provider was compromised to inject and execute remote malware (FakeUpdates/SocGholish) on over 250 media websites, enabling large-scale drive-by malware distribution to site visitors.

execution_context.trigger: When a user visits an affected media website and the compromised JavaScript is loaded by the browser
execution_context.file_location: Injected/compromised JavaScript file loaded from the media content provider's CDN (e.g., https://cdn.mediaprovider.com/compromised.js)
required_permissions: Potential access to browser storage (if subsequent payloads leverage it)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user visits an affected site, the compromised JavaScript executes in the browser, dynamically creates a <script> element with its src set to a malicious external domain, injects it into the DOM, and loads a remote payload, resulting in the execution of FakeUpdates malware on the user's system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code dynamically injects and executes a script from an external, non-affiliated domain at runtime, which is a well-known technique for delivering malware and is not expected in legitimate third-party JavaScript from a trusted provider.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate third-party JavaScript from a media content provider should only load resources from vetted, affiliated domains and should not inject scripts from unknown or newly registered external sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use cases may include loading analytics or advertising scripts from established, trusted partners, but never from domains unrelated to the provider or with no prior relationship.
key_indicators: Dynamic creation and injection of <script> tags referencing external domains
External script source domain is not associated with the media provider
Script loads additional JavaScript from infrastructure linked to FakeUpdates/SocGholish
Behavior matches known drive-by malware delivery patterns

attack_chain.action: Threat actor compromises the JavaScript code hosted by a trusted media content provider's CDN.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is distributed to all websites embedding the provider's code.

attack_chain.action: Compromised JavaScript is loaded by over 250 media websites and executed in visitors' browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious script injects and loads an additional payload from the attacker's infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: The injected payload (FakeUpdates/SocGholish) is executed in the user's browser, initiating malware delivery.
attack_chain.leads_to: User systems are exposed to and potentially infected with FakeUpdates malware.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected runtime injection of external scripts from non-affiliated or newly registered domains
JavaScript code dynamically creating <script> tags with src attributes pointing to untrusted remote sources
Execution of JavaScript that loads additional code from infrastructure associated with FakeUpdates/SocGholish
file_indicators: JavaScript files from trusted providers (e.g., CDN URLs) suddenly referencing or injecting new, unknown domains
Injected <script> tags in the DOM with src attributes pointing to suspicious or non-affiliated URLs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from media websites to domains associated with SocGholish/FakeUpdates campaigns
Unusual traffic patterns from user browsers to newly registered or flagged malicious domains after loading media content provider scripts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor and audit third-party JavaScript loaded by your site for unexpected changes, especially new or unrecognized external script sources. Use web application firewalls and browser security tools to detect and block dynamic script injection from untrusted domains. Analyze network traffic for connections to known FakeUpdates/SocGholish infrastructure and newly registered domains. Regularly verify the integrity of JavaScript dependencies and CDN-hosted assets to detect unauthorized modifications.
